papers.title: On Demand, Not Uniformity: Adaptive Expert Orchestration for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning (MCIT) enables Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to adapt to sequential instruction data while retaining previously acquired knowledge. While recent Mixture-of-Experts (MoE)-based methods mitigate forgetting by freezing historical experts and introducing new ones, they largely overlook the varying adaptation demands across tasks. Probing incoming tasks reveals pronounced heterogeneity in layer-wise gradient pressure and token-wise prediction difficulty. This observation highlights two unresolved decisions: where additional capacity is needed and how strongly new experts should contribute to individual tokens. To address both questions, we propose the Coverage-Calibrated Expert Injection and Residual Arbitration framework (CIRA-MoE), which derives expert acceptance margins via learnable threshold routing to serve as a unified coverage signal. Specifically, historical acceptance evidence guides the selective injection of new experts into insufficiently covered layers. Meanwhile, relative evidence between historical and current experts modulates token-wise residual contributions, coupled with arbitration-consistent regularization to promote expert specialization. Comprehensive experiments on UCIT and CoIN demonstrate that CIRA-MoE outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in MCIT.
papers.abstract_zh: 多模态持续指令微调（MCIT）使多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）能够适应序列化的指令数据，同时保留先前获得的知识。尽管近期基于混合专家（MoE）的方法通过冻结历史专家并引入新专家来缓解遗忘，但它们在很大程度上忽略了不同任务之间变化的适应需求。对传入任务的探测揭示了逐层梯度压力和逐token预测难度上的显著异质性。这一观察凸显了两个尚未解决的决策：何处需要额外容量，以及新专家应对单个token产生多强的贡献。为解决这两个问题，我们提出了覆盖校准专家注入与残差仲裁框架（CIRA-MoE），该框架通过可学习阈值路由推导专家接受边际，作为统一的覆盖信号。具体而言，历史接受证据指导将新专家选择性注入覆盖不足的层。同时，历史专家与当前专家之间的相对证据调节逐token的残差贡献，并结合仲裁一致性正则化以促进专家专业化。在UCIT和CoIN上的综合实验表明，CIRA-MoE在MCIT中优于现有最先进方法。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出CIRA-MoE框架，利用可学习阈值路由的覆盖信号指导新专家选择性注入覆盖不足的层，并按历史与当前专家的相对证据调节逐token残差贡献，在UCIT和CoIN上优于现有方法。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model
匹配 MLLM / VLM：multimodal large language model
匹配 预训练 / 后训练：instruction tuning
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: ProSE: Probing Reconstruction Error for Semantic-guided Expert Skipping in MoE-MLLMs
papers.abstract_en: Mixture-of-Experts Multimodal Large Language Models (MoE-MLLMs) offer scalable inference through sparse expert activation, yet substantial computational redundancy remains among the activated experts. Existing expert skipping methods typically calibrate thresholds based on target skipping ratios or final-output divergence, overlooking the accumulation of skipping-induced error across layers and the varying semantic importance of individual tokens. To address that, we propose ProSE, a training-free, semantic-guided expert skipping framework that probes layer-wise reconstruction error to promote representation consistency compared with default activation. Specifically, we construct query-aware semantic masks to identify salient visual tokens and progressively calibrate modality-specific skipping thresholds for each MoE layer. By minimizing masked reconstruction error under a given budget, ProSE maintains semantic consistency after skipping and allows adaptive expert allocation under limited activation budgets. Extensive experiments on 9 benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements on average over existing expert skipping methods, particularly under aggressive skipping settings. ProSE maintains over 96\% performance on KimiVL-A3B-Inst with 83\% expert skipping and accelerates prefilling by $1.7\times$.
papers.abstract_zh: 混合专家多模态大语言模型（MoE-MLLMs）通过稀疏专家激活实现可扩展推理，但被激活的专家之间仍存在大量计算冗余。现有专家跳过方法通常基于目标跳过比例或最终输出差异来校准阈值，忽略了跳过所引入误差在层间的累积以及单个token在语义重要性上的差异。为此，我们提出ProSE，一个无需训练、语义引导的专家跳过框架，它通过探测逐层重建误差来促进与默认激活相比的表示一致性。具体而言，我们构建查询感知的语义掩码以识别显著的视觉token，并为每个MoE层逐步校准模态特定的跳过阈值。通过在给定预算下最小化掩码重建误差，ProSE在跳过之后保持语义一致性，并允许在有限激活预算下进行自适应专家分配。在9个基准上的大量实验表明，相较于现有专家跳过方法，ProSE平均取得了一致提升，在激进跳过设置下尤为明显。ProSE在KimiVL-A3B-Inst上以83%的专家跳过率保持超过96%的性能，并将预填充加速1.7倍。
papers.tldr_zh: ProSE提出一种无需训练、语义引导的专家跳过框架，通过探测逐层重建误差并构建查询感知语义掩码来校准各MoE层的跳过阈值，在KimiVL-A3B-Inst上以83%跳过率保持96%以上性能并将预填充加速1.7倍。

匹配 MLLM / VLM：multimodal large language model

papers.title: MoMoVL: Modality-Aware Adaptive Compression for On-Device Sparsely-Activated Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract_en: The rise of the agentic web has been accompanied by growing demand for on-device Vision-Language Models (VLMs) that perform diverse cross-modal web tasks with enhanced privacy and reduced latency. Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models are widely adopted in modern VLMs for compute-efficient scalability, yet their multi-expert architecture poses deployment challenges due to substantial memory demands. Mixed-precision quantization is an effective compression technique that reduces bit-widths while adapting to the heterogeneous hardware budgets of edge devices, particularly well-suited for MoE due to its inherent structural sparsity, which causes imbalanced importance among experts. While prior work has applied quantization for efficient MoE inference at the edge, we point out that in MoE-based VLMs, the modality-specific characteristics of visual and text tokens further impact expert quantization. To address this issue, we present MoMoVL, a modality-aware adaptive compression framework for MoE-based VLMs that brings vision-language inference within reach of on-device resource budgets. Motivated by our empirical findings on modality-induced disparities across experts, MoMoVL jointly exploits the per-expert activation profile and per-modality quantization sensitivity to guide bit-width assignment. Experimental results show that MoMoVL improves the accuracy-compression trade-off relative to state-of-the-art mixed-precision baselines and reduces memory footprint by up to 15.44% with a modest drop in accuracy over its uniform-precision baseline. Our code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/sco-edge/MoMoVL.
papers.abstract_zh: 智能体网络的兴起伴随着对设备端视觉语言模型（VLMs）日益增长的需求，这些模型以更强的隐私性和更低的延迟执行多样化的跨模态网络任务。混合专家（MoE）模型因其计算高效的扩展性而被现代VLMs广泛采用，但其多专家架构因巨大的内存需求而带来部署挑战。混合精度量化是一种有效的压缩技术，可在降低位宽的同时适应边缘设备的异构硬件预算，尤其适合MoE，因为其固有的结构稀疏性导致专家间重要性不均衡。尽管先前工作已将量化用于边缘高效MoE推理，但我们指出，在基于MoE的VLMs中，视觉token和文本token的模态特定特性会进一步影响专家量化。为解决这一问题，我们提出MoMoVL，一种面向基于MoE的VLMs的模态感知自适应压缩框架，使视觉语言推理进入设备端资源预算范围。受我们对专家间模态引发差异的实证发现启发，MoMoVL联合利用逐专家激活画像和逐模态量化敏感度来指导位宽分配。实验结果表明，相对于最先进的混合精度基线，MoMoVL改善了精度-压缩权衡，并相较其均匀精度基线将内存占用最多降低15.44%，精度仅有适度下降。我们的代码和数据公开于https://github.com/sco-edge/MoMoVL。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出MoMoVL模态感知自适应压缩框架，联合利用逐专家激活画像与逐模态量化敏感度分配位宽，在精度适度下降下将内存占用最多降低15.44%。
why_it_matters: 匹配 MLLM / VLM：vision-language model, vlm
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Deep Learning for Physicists: From Linear Regression to Reasoning Models
papers.abstract_en: These lecture notes are based on an introductory course on neural networks and deep learning that the author taught in the School of Mathematical Sciences at Queen Mary University of London in 2023/24 and 2024/25. The author, however, is a physicist, and it shows: wherever possible, ideas are explained with physical intuition rather than heavy formalism. Readers with a background in physics or mathematics who want a self-contained, introductory route into modern machine learning may therefore find these notes particularly friendly. The notes start from maximum likelihood, least squares, linear regression and (stochastic) gradient descent. They then cover neural networks, backpropagation, the vanishing gradient problem, batch and layer normalization, overfitting and regularization, adversarial examples, and the kernel method. The second half turns to natural language processing: word embeddings, recurrent networks and LSTMs, the attention mechanism and Transformers, and large language models, including scaling laws, the history of GPT, instruction tuning, reinforcement learning from human feedback, hallucination, alignment faking, chain-of-thought reasoning and test-time scaling. The emphasis on large language models reflects requests from the students. The notes are aimed at third- and fourth-year students in the UK system. Because the course was also taken by students from other departments, very little is assumed: even basic material such as matrix multiplication is explained from scratch, so readers familiar with it can safely skip such parts. No originality is claimed; the aim is a coherent, intuitive path through the material. Developments after spring 2025 are not covered, but the basic ideas emphasized here are unlikely to go out of date soon.
papers.abstract_zh: 这些讲义基于作者2023/24和2024/25学年在伦敦玛丽女王大学数学科学学院讲授的一门神经网络与深度学习入门课程。然而，作者是一名物理学家，这一点显而易见：在可能之处，概念以物理直觉而非繁重形式化来解释。因此，具有物理或数学背景、希望获得自包含的现代机器学习入门路径的读者可能会觉得这些讲义格外友好。讲义从最大似然、最小二乘、线性回归和（随机）梯度下降开始，随后涵盖神经网络、反向传播、梯度消失问题、批归一化与层归一化、过拟合与正则化、对抗样本以及核方法。后半部分转向自然语言处理：词嵌入、循环网络与LSTM、注意力机制与Transformer，以及大语言模型，包括缩放定律、GPT的历史、指令微调、基于人类反馈的强化学习、幻觉、对齐伪装、思维链推理和测试时缩放。对大语言模型的侧重反映了学生的要求。讲义面向英国学制的三、四年级学生。由于该课程也有其他院系的学生选修，因此假设极少：甚至矩阵乘法等基础材料也从头讲解，熟悉这些内容的读者可以安全跳过。不主张原创性；目标是提供一条连贯、直观的材料学习路径。2025年春季之后的发展未涵盖，但此处强调的基本思想不太可能很快过时。
papers.tldr_zh: 该讲义以物理直觉为主线，从最大似然、线性回归与梯度下降讲到神经网络、Transformer与大语言模型（含缩放定律、指令微调、RLHF、思维链与测试时缩放），为物理或数学背景读者提供自包含的深度学习入门路径。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model, transformer
匹配 预训练 / 后训练：instruction tuning, reinforcement learning from human feedback
匹配 模型架构：attention mechanism
偏好加分 scaling-and-compute：scaling law, scaling laws
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: SpecLook: Speculating Where to Look for Fast and Reliable Agentic MLLMs
papers.abstract_en: Agentic multimodal large language models (MLLMs) that think with images interleave reasoning with zoom-in tool calls. However, this sequential loop is slow, and its answers carry no reliability score. Prior speculation of tokens, reasoning steps, or answers keeps the loop, and answer speculation also accepts confident errors. We find that the loop mostly adds one zoom-in step, with which a small model is ahead of the agent on most splits. Our key insight is to speculate the agent's next observation, which, unlike a drafted answer, can be verified, corrected, and used to test the answer. We propose SpecLook, a training-free speculate-and-verify framework with three levels. A small model drafts a glimpse and re-answers from it, and the question ends if the answer is unchanged and confident. Otherwise, the agent's large model verifies and corrects the glimpse without tools, and their answers are fused. Only questions that still lack evidence reach the agent, in one forward pass that SpecLook-Fast skips, so no question runs the loop. The trace scores every answer's reliability without labels. Extensive experiments on V*, HR-Bench, and POPE show that both are more accurate than every baseline on every split. SpecLook reaches 87.2% and 86.2% mean accuracy with 7.7x and 4.7x speedups over the DeepEyes-7B and Thyme-RL agents, and SpecLook-Fast reaches 9.9x and 6.3x.
papers.abstract_zh: 以图像思考的智能体多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）将推理与放大工具调用交错进行。然而，这一顺序循环速度慢，且其答案不携带可靠性分数。先前对token、推理步骤或答案的推测仍保留该循环，且答案推测还会接受自信的错误。我们发现该循环大多只增加一个放大步骤，而小模型在大多数划分上领先于智能体。我们的关键洞见是推测智能体的下一个观察，与草拟答案不同，该观察可被验证、纠正并用于检验答案。我们提出SpecLook，一个免训练的三级推测-验证框架。小模型草拟一个瞥见并据此重新作答，若答案不变且置信则问题结束。否则，智能体的大模型在无工具条件下验证并纠正该瞥见，并融合二者的答案。只有仍缺乏证据的问题才到达智能体，且仅需一次前向传播，SpecLook-Fast会跳过该传播，因此没有问题是运行循环的。该轨迹无需标签即可为每个答案的可靠性打分。在V*、HR-Bench和POPE上的大量实验表明，二者在每个划分上均比所有基线更准确。SpecLook在DeepEyes-7B和Thyme-RL智能体上分别以7.7倍和4.7倍加速达到87.2%和86.2%的平均准确率，SpecLook-Fast则达到9.9倍和6.3倍。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出免训练的SpecLook推测-验证框架，通过小模型草拟并验证智能体的下一个观察而非答案，在V*、HR-Bench和POPE上以最高9.9倍加速取得更高准确率。

匹配 MLLM / VLM：multimodal large language model
evidence: 实验或理论证据信号：extensive experiment

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Vision-Language Fusion
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language models (VLMs) have emerged as central foundation models combining multimodal perception with text comprehension. While VLMs are traditionally built via late fusion by continued pre-training an off-the-shelf language model on multimodal (image-text) data, mixing modalities from the start of pre-training (early fusion) has recently gained traction. However, the fundamental trade-offs between these paradigms remain poorly understood, resulting in expensive and heuristic-driven training recipes. In this paper, we systematically analyze the learning dynamics of these multimodal pre-training processes, showing that validation losses during vision-language fusion can be modeled by separating the base learning trajectory, where different data types contribute at distinct rates, from a distribution shift driven by the competition between modalities. We derive a scaling law that unifiedly describes these dynamics, enabling accurate loss predictions across mixture ratios, training steps, and model sizes. Crucially, our law characterizes the trade-off between early and late fusion: under a fixed data budget, early fusion preserves text performance while late fusion favors vision performance, yielding a trade-off that increasingly tilts toward early fusion as model size scales. Extensive experiments confirm that our scaling law reliably captures multimodal learning dynamics and governs fusion decisions.
papers.abstract_zh: 视觉-语言模型（VLMs）已成为结合多模态感知与文本理解的核心基础模型。传统上，VLMs通过在多模态（图像-文本）数据上继续预训练现成语言模型来实现晚期融合，而从一开始预训练就混合模态（早期融合）近来受到关注。然而，这些范式之间的基本权衡仍鲜为人知，导致训练配方昂贵且依赖启发式。本文系统分析了这些多模态预训练过程的学习动态，表明视觉-语言融合过程中的验证损失可以通过将基础学习轨迹（不同数据类型以不同速率贡献）与由模态间竞争驱动的分布偏移分离来建模。我们推导出一个统一描述这些动态的缩放定律，能够跨混合比例、训练步数和模型规模准确预测损失。关键的是，我们的定律刻画了早期融合与晚期融合之间的权衡：在固定数据预算下，早期融合保持文本性能而晚期融合有利于视觉性能，且随着模型规模扩大，该权衡日益偏向早期融合。大量实验证实，我们的缩放定律可靠地捕捉多模态学习动态并指导融合决策。
papers.tldr_zh: 该文将视觉-语言融合的验证损失建模为基础学习轨迹与模态竞争所致分布偏移的分离，推导出跨混合比例、训练步数和模型规模的统一缩放定律，并揭示固定数据预算下早期融合保文本性能、晚期融合利视觉性能且随模型规模增大权衡偏向早期融合。

匹配 MLLM / VLM：vision-language model, vlm
匹配 预训练 / 后训练：pre-training

papers.title: QDA: Closed-Loop LLM Quantization Design with Agents
papers.abstract_en: Post-training quantization is the standard way to serve large language models at low cost. However, the best quantization recipe differs across models and precisions. As a result, experts must redesign it for every new model, which is time-consuming and often sub-optimal. Fortunately, an LLM agent can take over this design by refining the recipe over rounds of building and evaluating candidates, so that more rounds lead to better recipes. However, evaluating one quantized reasoning model takes tens of GPU-hours, and combining methods from different codebases means porting each to the new architecture by hand. We present QDA, a system in which an agent designs the recipe for each model and precision. To make evaluation fast, QDA scores each candidate in minutes by its output KL divergence from the original model on reasoning traces that the agent never sees, and checks promising ones with long generations to catch failures such as repetition loops. To make building fast, QDA provides a library of public PTQ methods that are compatible with one another and with new model architectures. Across four reasoning models, QDA improves accuracy over the strongest public recipe by 0.9, 1.4 and 2.2 percentage points on average at W4A16, W4A8 and W3A16, using 64 GPU-hours per search. On the 320B-parameter MoE model GLM-5.3-Flash at NVFP4 W4A4, it recovers 98.3% of the FP8 model's accuracy, against 96.9% for the best vendor checkpoint. Every QDA checkpoint also runs on existing serving kernels with no inference overhead. We will release the library, the evaluator and the harness.
papers.abstract_zh: 训练后量化是低成本服务大语言模型的标准方式。然而，最佳量化配方因模型和精度而异。因此，专家必须为每个新模型重新设计，这耗时且往往次优。幸运的是，LLM智能体可以通过多轮构建和评估候选来接管这一设计，使更多轮次带来更好的配方。然而，评估一个量化推理模型需要数十个GPU小时，而组合来自不同代码库的方法意味着需手工将每种方法移植到新架构。我们提出QDA，一个由智能体为每个模型和精度设计配方的系统。为加快评估，QDA通过在智能体从未见过的推理轨迹上计算候选相对原始模型的输出KL散度，在数分钟内为其打分，并用长生成检查有前景的候选以捕捉重复循环等失败。为加快构建，QDA提供相互兼容且兼容新模型架构的公开PTQ方法库。在四个推理模型上，QDA在W4A16、W4A8和W3A16下相较最强公开配方平均提升准确率0.9、1.4和2.2个百分点，每次搜索使用64 GPU小时。在320B参数的MoE模型GLM-5.3-Flash的NVFP4 W4A4下，它恢复了FP8模型准确率的98.3%，而最佳厂商检查点为96.9%。每个QDA检查点还可在现有服务内核上运行，无推理开销。我们将发布该库、评估器与测试框架。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出QDA系统，由LLM智能体通过KL散度快速评估与兼容PTQ方法库迭代设计量化配方，在四个推理模型上平均提升准确率最高2.2个百分点，并在GLM-5.3-Flash上恢复FP8准确率的98.3%。

匹配 预训练 / 后训练：post-training
匹配 模型架构：model architecture

papers.title: Communicate the Change: Efficient Expert Parallelism via Activation Compression
papers.abstract_en: Scaling has driven the success of large language models (LLM), with sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures enabling greater parameter capacity without a proportional increase in computation. At large scales, MoE models rely on expert parallelism to distribute experts across devices. Each MoE layer requires two synchronous collective communication steps during inference: dispatching hidden states to the activated experts and combining the resulting expert outputs. As compute throughput has outpaced interconnect bandwidth, these synchronous collectives have become a major bottleneck to MoE scaling and efficiency. We address this challenge with EchoMoE, a lightweight architecture modification that retrofits existing MoE models, requiring approximately 8,500x fewer training tokens than full pretraining. Motivated by the observation that transformer blocks update the residual stream incrementally, we use a hidden state from an earlier layer as a reference and communicate only the compressed difference between it and the current state, rather than communicating each hidden state in full. EchoMoE periodically refreshes these reference states and transmits only the compressed differences synchronously, reducing the traffic on latency-critical paths without significant computational overhead. EchoMoE reduces inter-node communication volume by 58% and improves throughput by 22.6%, while preserving average performance within 3.8 percentage points across 18 benchmarks. EchoMoE further improves inference throughput by up to 2.38x over bandwidth-constrained Ethernet, paving the way for wide-area distributed inference. EchoMoE also tolerates quantization of the communicated representations without measurable quality loss. We release an efficient implementation for applying EchoMoE to pretrained MoE models, together with an inference integration for vLLM.
papers.abstract_zh: 规模化推动了大语言模型（LLM）的成功，稀疏混合专家（MoE）架构使参数容量得以提升而计算量不必成比例增加。在大规模下，MoE模型依赖专家并行将专家分布到各设备。每个MoE层在推理期间需要两个同步集合通信步骤：将隐藏状态分发到被激活的专家，以及合并得到的专家输出。随着计算吞吐超过互连带宽，这些同步集合通信已成为MoE扩展与效率的主要瓶颈。我们通过EchoMoE应对这一挑战，这是一种轻量级架构修改，可改造现有MoE模型，所需训练token比完整预训练少约8,500倍。受Transformer块增量更新残差流这一观察的启发，我们使用来自较早层的隐藏状态作为参考，仅通信其与当前状态之间的压缩差异，而非完整通信每个隐藏状态。EchoMoE定期刷新这些参考状态，并仅同步传输压缩差异，从而减少延迟关键路径上的流量且无显著计算开销。EchoMoE将节点间通信量减少58%，吞吐提升22.6%，同时在18个基准上平均性能保持在3.8个百分点以内。在带宽受限的以太网上，EchoMoE进一步将推理吞吐提升至多2.38倍，为广域分布式推理铺平道路。EchoMoE还能容忍所通信表示的量化而无明显质量损失。我们发布了将EchoMoE应用于预训练MoE模型的高效实现，以及面向vLLM的推理集成。
papers.tldr_zh: EchoMoE利用Transformer块增量更新残差流的特性，以较早层隐藏状态为参考仅同步传输压缩差异并定期刷新参考状态，将节点间通信量减少58%、吞吐提升22.6%，在18个基准上平均性能损失不超过3.8个百分点。

papers.title: TeleChat to Xing4: Advancing Frontier Agentic Models on Domestic Chips and Frameworks
papers.abstract_en: We present Xing 4, a series of large language models that extends the TeleChat lineage through coordinated advances in model architecture and training infrastructure on Ascend. This report describes the design principles and systems engineering behind the series, spanning architecture selection, large-scale pretraining, and reasoning and agentic post-training. We study how sparse activation, attention design, model depth and width, and speculative decoding balance model capacity with computation, memory access, and execution overhead. Our pretraining infrastructure builds on MindSpore HyperParallel, combining topology-aware hybrid sharding, efficient distributed optimizer execution, and coordinated management of long-sequence workloads and activation memory. CPU affinity and core isolation further reduce host scheduling interference. Together, these mechanisms support the pretraining of a 285B-parameter model on 8,192 Ascend 910C cards, providing a concrete setting for the architectural and systems studies. For post-training, we introduce TeleGym, a unified agent execution platform that connects execution, evaluation, and trajectory construction to policy optimization. Disaggregated asynchronous execution, bounded oversampling, and partial rollout accommodate heterogeneous task durations while preserving trajectory continuity across policy updates. Together, these advances establish an Ascend-oriented training foundation for the continued development of Xing 4 across model scales and increasingly demanding reasoning and agent workloads.
papers.abstract_zh: 我们提出Xing 4，一系列大语言模型，通过在昇腾上模型架构与训练基础设施的协同进步扩展了TeleChat谱系。本报告描述了该系列背后的设计原则与系统工程，涵盖架构选择、大规模预训练以及推理与智能体后训练。我们研究了稀疏激活、注意力设计、模型深度与宽度以及推测解码如何平衡模型容量与计算、内存访问和执行开销。我们的预训练基础设施构建于MindSpore HyperParallel之上，结合拓扑感知混合分片、高效分布式优化器执行以及对长序列工作负载和激活内存的协调管理。CPU亲和性与核心隔离进一步减少了主机调度干扰。这些机制共同支持在8,192张昇腾910C卡上预训练一个285B参数模型，为架构与系统研究提供了具体场景。在后训练方面，我们引入TeleGym，一个统一的智能体执行平台，将执行、评估和轨迹构建与策略优化连接起来。分离式异步执行、有界过采样和部分回放适应异构任务时长，同时在策略更新之间保持轨迹连续性。这些进展共同为Xing 4在模型规模和日益苛刻的推理与智能体工作负载上的持续发展建立了面向昇腾的训练基础。
papers.tldr_zh: 该报告介绍Xing 4系列大语言模型，基于MindSpore HyperParallel在8,192张昇腾910C卡上预训练285B参数模型，并引入TeleGym智能体执行平台，通过分离式异步执行与部分回放等机制支持推理与智能体后训练。

papers.title: As Student Rollouts Continue, Visual Backdoors Keep Growing
papers.abstract_en: Conventional knowledge distillation can facilitate the propagation of backdoors from teacher models to student models. However, how this risk manifests in On-Policy Distillation (OPD) remains insufficiently studied. OPD has recently emerged as an important post-training paradigm for Vision-Language Models (VLMs). Unlike traditional offline distillation, OPD does not require teacher-generated responses. Instead, it uses the teacher's probability distributions to supervise response trajectories generated online by the student. Since the initial student model typically generates benign responses and receives no explicit supervision from malicious target responses, OPD appears to offer some inherent resistance to backdoor propagation. In this paper, we challenge this intuition and reveal a more subtle risk of visual backdoor propagation in OPD. Through experiments across multiple model families and datasets, together with theoretical analysis, we identify three main findings. First, unlike the relatively gradual propagation observed in traditional offline distillation, backdoors rarely emerge in OPD at low poisoning ratios. However, the attack success rate rapidly approaches 100% once a critical threshold is exceeded. Second, backdoor propagation does not depend on explicit malicious responses. Instead, it is driven by the continuous accumulation of anomalous probability mass assigned by the teacher. Finally, based on these findings, we propose a novel trigger design that enables visual backdoor propagation with zero explicit trigger injection. These findings further reveal an overlooked mechanism of backdoor propagation in OPD and highlight its potential security risks.
papers.abstract_zh: 传统知识蒸馏可能促使后门从教师模型传播到学生模型。然而，这种风险在在线策略蒸馏（On-Policy Distillation, OPD）中如何表现，仍缺乏充分研究。OPD 近来已成为视觉语言模型（VLM）的重要后训练范式。与传统离线蒸馏不同，OPD 不需要教师生成的回答，而是利用教师的概率分布来监督学生在线生成的回答轨迹。由于初始学生模型通常生成良性回答，且不会收到来自恶意目标回答的显式监督，OPD 似乎对后门传播具有一定内在抵抗力。本文挑战这一直觉，揭示了 OPD 中视觉后门传播更隐蔽的风险。通过跨多个模型家族和数据集的实验以及理论分析，我们得到三个主要发现。第一，与传统离线蒸馏中相对渐进的传播不同，OPD 在低投毒比例下很少出现后门；然而一旦超过临界阈值，攻击成功率会迅速接近 100%。第二，后门传播不依赖显式的恶意回答，而是由教师分配的异常概率质量的持续累积所驱动。最后，基于这些发现，我们提出一种新的触发器设计，可在零显式触发器注入的情况下实现视觉后门传播。这些发现进一步揭示了 OPD 中被忽视的后门传播机制，并凸显其潜在安全风险。
papers.tldr_zh: 研究发现在线策略蒸馏中视觉后门在低投毒比例下很少出现，但超过临界阈值后攻击成功率迅速接近100%，其传播由教师异常概率质量的累积驱动，并提出零显式触发器注入的触发器设计。

匹配 预训练 / 后训练：post-training

papers.title: Harvesting Expert-Parallel Bubbles for Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract_en: GPUs are expensive, yet latency-critical large language model (LLM) inference leaves part of them idle. Colocation reclaims this capacity by running best-effort work, such as fine-tuning, alongside serving. Many leading LLMs now use a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture, which adds a new source of idle time. Under expert parallelism, MoE experts are spread across GPUs, and because the router sends uneven numbers of tokens to each GPU, lightly loaded GPUs wait for the most loaded one. Even after applying load balancing solutions, such bubbles still take 8--13% of prefill time. We present BubbleTea, the first colocation system that leverages expert-parallel bubbles for fine-tuning. Unlike existing colocation systems, which make one scheduling decision for all GPUs per forward pass, BubbleTea predicts each GPU's bubble at every layer from the router's token assignment, and fills it with short chunks of fine-tuning work that reuse the weights already loaded for serving. We also introduce compiler passes that automatically derive these chunks from the served LLM as-is, without porting each model architecture to a separate training engine. Our evaluation on three MoE models, served on four A100 GPUs, shows that fine-tuning throughput with BubbleTea is 1.9--6.2$\times$ faster than with LLMStation, a state-of-the-art colocation system. BubbleTea keeps p90 inference latency within 10% of serving alone in 50 of 63 workloads, compared to 44 for LLMStation. On bursty production traces, BubbleTea trains 3.3$\times$ faster than LLMStation and 14$\times$ faster than a stock trainer colocated under CUDA MPS, with p90 inference latency staying within 7% of serving alone.
papers.abstract_zh: GPU昂贵，然而延迟关键的大语言模型（LLM）推理使部分GPU处于空闲。共置通过运行尽力而为的工作（如微调）与服务工作负载并行来回收这一容量。许多领先LLM现采用混合专家（MoE）架构，这增加了新的空闲时间来源。在专家并行下，MoE专家分布在各GPU上，且由于路由器向每个GPU发送的token数不均，轻负载GPU需等待负载最重的GPU。即使应用负载均衡方案，此类气泡仍占预填充时间的8--13%。我们提出BubbleTea，首个利用专家并行气泡进行微调的共置系统。与现有共置系统每次前向传播对所有GPU做一次调度决策不同，BubbleTea根据路由器的token分配预测每个GPU在每一层的气泡，并用复用已为服务加载权重的短微调工作块填充它。我们还引入编译器遍，可自动从原样服务的LLM推导这些工作块，而无需将每个模型架构移植到单独的训练引擎。我们在四块A100 GPU上服务三个MoE模型的评估表明，BubbleTea的微调吞吐量比最先进共置系统LLMStation快1.9--6.2倍。BubbleTea在63个工作负载中的50个上将p90推理延迟保持在单独服务的10%以内，而LLMStation为44个。在突发生产轨迹上，BubbleTea训练速度比LLMStation快3.3倍，比在CUDA MPS下共置的现成训练器快14倍，且p90推理延迟保持在单独服务的7%以内。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出BubbleTea共置系统，按路由器token分配逐层预测各GPU的专家并行气泡并填充复用服务权重的微调工作块，微调吞吐量比LLMStation快1.9--6.2倍。

papers.title: Reference-Guided Data Curation for 3D Medical Vision-Language Pretraining
papers.abstract_en: Training 3D vision-language models (VLMs) on large medical imaging datasets collected across institutions is constrained by data quality. Vast, uncurated pools of image-report pairs are characterized by redundancy, class imbalance, and cross-institutional heterogeneity. We address this challenge of data curation for improving 3D VLM pretraining by proposing an offline, training-free, reference-guided data curation recipe. Our approach leverages a small, high-quality reference set to independently extract quality signals for each modality of a large, uncurated pool and merges them through a rank-aggregation step into a single ranking that guides sample selection. We validate this method on datasets comprising 35k 3D abdominal CT volume-report pairs from two institutions and 58k 2D chest X-ray image-report pairs. On 3D CT, using our reference-guided data curation strategy, our curated model matches the zero-shot disease classification performance of a state-of-the-art baseline (Merlin) while using $3.3\times$ less training data and a reference set of 5k samples. On 2D chest X-rays, our method yields a curated model that matches or exceeds the zero-shot disease classification performance of a model trained on the full pool while using up to $10\times$ less training data and a reference set of only 74 samples. Ablations show that the selection is stable under resampling of the reference, that smaller reference sets still outperform random sampling, and that label rebalancing does not improve performance. To support reproducibility, we release our code.
papers.abstract_zh: 在跨机构收集的大规模医学影像数据集上训练3D视觉-语言模型（VLM）受限于数据质量。大量未经整理的图像-报告对具有冗余、类别不平衡和跨机构异质性等特点。我们针对改进3D VLM预训练的数据整理难题，提出一种离线、免训练、参考引导的数据整理方案。该方法利用一个小规模高质量参考集，为大规模未整理池中每个模态独立提取质量信号，并通过秩聚合步骤将其合并为单一排序以指导样本选择。我们在包含来自两个机构的35k个3D腹部CT体数据-报告对以及58k个2D胸部X射线图像-报告对的数据集上验证了该方法。在3D CT上，采用我们的参考引导数据整理策略，整理后的模型在使用3.3倍更少训练数据和5k样本参考集的情况下，达到了最先进基线（Merlin）的零样本疾病分类性能。在2D胸部X射线上，我们的方法得到的整理模型在使用最多10倍更少训练数据和仅74个样本的参考集的情况下，达到或超过在全量池上训练模型的零样本疾病分类性能。消融实验表明，选择在参考集重采样下是稳定的，更小的参考集仍优于随机采样，且标签重平衡并未提升性能。为支持可复现性，我们发布了代码。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出一种离线免训练的参考引导数据整理方法，利用小规模高质量参考集为大规模未整理医学图像-报告对生成质量排序以筛选样本，在3D腹部CT和2D胸部X射线数据上以显著更少的训练数据达到或超过基线零样本疾病分类性能。

papers.title: PhysScope: Agentic Multimodal Physics Reasoning with Grounded Visual Memory
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language models (VLMs) can correctly interpret physics diagrams yet apply constraints outside the states or conditions in which they hold, causing premise errors to propagate through subsequent calculations. We introduce PhysScope, an inference-time visual harness that supports self-correction of these scope mismatches without updating model weights. PhysScope enables the model to link physical scopes directly to its visual observations and explicitly constructs derived views to support reasoning. The harness imposes explicit constraints on state distinctions, conditions, and physical scopes during model reasoning, and checks agent-proposed revisions against sources and scopes. Accepted revisions invalidate registered dependents, thereby maintaining scope-aware working memory. On PhysAlign, PhysScope achieves higher solving scores than direct solving across all six evaluated VLMs. With Gemini-3.8-flash, it outperforms Canvas-CoT by 9.34 percentage points and substantially improves solving accuracy on the out-of-distribution (OOD) PhysUniBench benchmark. Ablation studies support explicit scope management and dependency maintenance as design principles for multimodal physics reasoning agents.
papers.abstract_zh: 视觉语言模型（VLM）能够正确解读物理图示，却会在其不成立的状态或条件之外应用约束，导致前提错误传播到后续计算中。我们提出 PhysScope，一种推理时的视觉约束框架，支持在不更新模型权重的情况下对这些作用域不匹配进行自我纠正。PhysScope 使模型能够将物理作用域直接关联到其视觉观察，并显式构造派生视图以支持推理。该框架在模型推理过程中对状态区分、条件和物理作用域施加显式约束，并对照来源与作用域检查智能体提出的修订。被接受的修订会使已注册的依赖项失效，从而维护作用域感知的工作记忆。在 PhysAlign 上，PhysScope 在全部六个被评估的 VLM 上取得了高于直接求解的解题得分。使用 Gemini-3.8-flash 时，它比 Canvas-CoT 高出 9.34 个百分点，并在分布外（OOD）的 PhysUniBench 基准上显著提升了解题准确率。消融研究支持将显式作用域管理和依赖维护作为多模态物理推理智能体的设计原则。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出推理时视觉约束框架PhysScope，通过显式作用域管理、派生视图构造与依赖失效机制实现自我纠正，在PhysAlign上六个VLM均优于直接求解，Gemini-3.8-flash下比Canvas-CoT高9.34个百分点。

limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Ultimate3D: Teaching Multimodal LLMs 3D Camera-Object Relations by Large-Scale Visual Instruction Data
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) struggle with accurately capturing camera-object relations, especially for object orientation, camera viewpoint, and camera shots. This stems from the fact that existing MLLMs are trained on images with limited diverse camera-object relations and corresponding textual descriptions. To address this, we propose a synthetic generation pipeline to create large-scale 3D visual instruction datasets. Our framework takes 3D assets as input and uses rendering and diffusion-based image generation models to create photorealistic images preserving precise camera-object relations. Additionally, large language models (LLMs) are used to generate text prompts for guiding visual instruction tuning and controlling image generation. We create Ultimate3D, a large-scale 3D-grounded 2D visual instruction dataset. Ultimate3D consists of 240K VQAs with precise camera-object annotations, and corresponding benchmark. MLLMs fine-tuned on our proposed dataset outperform commercial models by a large margin, achieving an average accuracy improvement of 29.7% on camera-object relation recognition tasks. Our code, dataset, and benchmark will contribute to broad MLLM applications.
papers.abstract_zh: 多模态大语言模型（MLLM）在准确捕捉相机-物体关系方面存在困难，尤其是物体朝向、相机视角和相机镜头类型。这源于现有MLLM训练所用图像中相机-物体关系多样性有限且缺乏相应文本描述。为解决这一问题，我们提出一种合成生成流水线，用于创建大规模3D视觉指令数据集。我们的框架以3D资产为输入，使用渲染和基于扩散的图像生成模型来创建保持精确相机-物体关系的照片级真实图像。此外，使用大语言模型（LLM）生成文本提示，以指导视觉指令微调并控制图像生成。我们构建了Ultimate3D，一个大规模基于3D的2D视觉指令数据集。Ultimate3D包含240K个具有精确相机-物体标注的VQA，以及相应的基准。在我们提出的数据集上微调的MLLM大幅优于商业模型，在相机-物体关系识别任务上平均准确率提升29.7%。我们的代码、数据集和基准将有助于广泛的MLLM应用。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出以3D资产为输入的合成生成流水线，结合渲染、扩散模型和LLM生成保持精确相机-物体关系的图像与文本指令，构建含240K VQA的Ultimate3D数据集及基准，微调后的MLLM在相机-物体关系识别任务上平均准确率提升29.7%。

匹配 MLLM / VLM：multimodal large language model

papers.title: DAQ: Decision-Aligned Post-Training Quantization for Spiking Transformers
papers.abstract_en: Spiking transformers combine attention-based representation learning with sparse spike communication, yet their weights and membrane variables still incur substantial storage and computation overhead. Post-training quantization (PTQ) offers a practical way to reduce these overheads, but preserving neuronal firing under weight and membrane quantization remains challenging. In this paper, we propose Decision-Aligned Post-Training Quantization (DAQ), a method that calibrates the quantizers to align neuronal firing decisions with those of a floating-point reference. We analyze how errors from these quantizers affect firing at decision boundaries and how they propagate over time steps in recurrent neurons. Based on this analysis, we formulate an objective that encourages quantized membrane variables to remain within the reference firing regions along the quantized model's own state trajectory. Experiments across multiple spiking transformer architectures on image classification, semantic segmentation, and event-based tracking demonstrate the effectiveness of DAQ with 4-bit weights and membrane variables. On FE108, DAQ achieves 58.8\% AUC and 90.9\% PR with SDTrack, while reducing energy by 66.2\%.
papers.abstract_zh: 脉冲Transformer将基于注意力的表示学习与稀疏脉冲通信相结合，但其权重和膜变量仍带来大量存储与计算开销。训练后量化（PTQ）为降低这些开销提供了实用途径，但在权重和膜量化下保持神经元发放仍具挑战。本文提出决策对齐训练后量化（Decision-Aligned Post-Training Quantization, DAQ），一种通过校准量化器使神经元发放决策与浮点参考对齐的方法。我们分析了这些量化器的误差如何影响决策边界处的发放，以及误差如何在循环神经元中随时间步传播。基于该分析，我们构建了一个目标，促使量化后的膜变量沿量化模型自身的状态轨迹保持在参考发放区域内。在图像分类、语义分割和基于事件的跟踪任务上跨多种脉冲Transformer架构的实验表明，DAQ 在 4 位权重和膜变量下有效。在 FE108 上，DAQ 配合 SDTrack 取得 58.8% AUC 和 90.9% PR，同时降低 66.2% 能耗。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出决策对齐训练后量化DAQ，通过校准量化器使脉冲发放决策对齐浮点参考并约束膜变量沿自身状态轨迹处于参考发放区域，在4位权重与膜变量下于分类、分割和事件跟踪任务上有效，FE108上降低66.2%能耗。

papers.title: NaviGATE: Noise-Aware Dual-View Generation for Multimodal Knowledge Graph Reasoning
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal knowledge graph reasoning (MKGR) aims to infer missing facts by jointly exploiting relational structures, textual descriptions, and visual evidence. Existing embedding-based methods effectively capture graph topology, but their fixed multimodal representations are less effective for query-specific fine-grained semantic reasoning, while generation-based methods are vulnerable to noisy retrieval and may produce invalid entities. To address these challenges, we propose NaviGATE, a noise-aware generative framework for MKGR. NaviGATE first aligns graph-derived structural representations with textual semantics, then performs structure-aware internal knowledge activation by fine-tuning the multimodal language model with multimodal entity summaries and injected structural tokens. In the noise-aware dual-view instruction tuning stage, NaviGATE jointly optimizes retrieval-free and retrieval-aware views: reliable retrieved candidates are reinforced through contrastive logit sharpening, while misleading candidates are suppressed through parametric consistency distillation. In inference, structure-constrained decoding restricts generation to valid entities in the target knowledge graph. Experiments on standard benchmarks show that NaviGATE consistently outperforms strong unimodal, multimodal, and generation-based baselines, and remains robust under noisy retrieval scenarios.

papers.title: LoopZip: Visual Token Compression for Efficient Looped Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Looped vision-language models (VLMs) deepen computation by reusing shared layers, approaching larger models' capabilities with fewer parameters and easing the storage and deployment burden of stacking independent layers. However, repeatedly processing long visual sequences still incurs substantial compute and GPU memory costs. Visual token compression reduces these costs by shortening sequences. Existing methods mainly select original tokens directly or combine selection with aggregation. In looped models, the former may overlook changing token importance across calls and discard information needed later; the latter lack joint consideration of output changes across calls, limiting information preservation. We propose LoopZip, a training-free visual token compression algorithm addressing both issues. Visual aggregation builds a compact candidate pool before the looped backbone, and cross-invocation selection averages instruction attention from the first two existing calls of the same shared attention layer to retain tokens needed by both states. Weight-tied value correction then jointly fits shared visual-value adjustments to both pre-selection layer outputs, reducing output deviations across states. To validate LoopZip's effectiveness, we conduct extensive experiments covering two open-source looped VLMs, eleven benchmarks, and three pruning ratios. On LoopVL-1B, LoopZip retains 97.16% of the original model's performance at 50% pruning ratio and exceeds the strongest baseline by 5.36% at 87.5% pruning ratio. Across Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, and SGLang, LoopVL-1B with LoopZip reduces peak allocated GPU memory by 58.36%-58.98% and achieves 2.01-2.47x end-to-end speedups over the original model.
papers.abstract_zh: 循环视觉语言模型（VLM）通过复用共享层来加深计算，以更少参数逼近更大模型的能力，并缓解堆叠独立层带来的存储与部署负担。然而，反复处理长视觉序列仍会带来大量计算和 GPU 内存开销。视觉 token 压缩通过缩短序列来降低这些开销。现有方法主要直接选择原始 token，或将选择与聚合相结合。在循环模型中，前者可能忽略不同调用间 token 重要性的变化，并丢弃后续所需的信息；后者缺乏对不同调用间输出变化的联合考虑，限制了信息保留。我们提出 LoopZip，一种无需训练的视觉 token 压缩算法，同时解决上述两个问题。视觉聚合在循环主干之前构建紧凑候选池，跨调用选择对同一共享注意力层前两次现有调用的指令注意力取平均，以保留两种状态都需要的 token。权重共享的值校正随后联合拟合共享视觉值调整，使其同时适配选择前层的两种输出，从而减小不同状态间的输出偏差。为验证 LoopZip 的有效性，我们开展了大量实验，覆盖两个开源循环 VLM、十一个基准和三种剪枝比例。在 LoopVL-1B 上，LoopZip 在 50% 剪枝比例下保留原模型 97.16% 的性能，在 87.5% 剪枝比例下超过最强基线 5.36%。在 Hugging Face Transformers、vLLM 和 SGLang 上，使用 LoopZip 的 LoopVL-1B 将峰值分配 GPU 内存降低 58.36%-58.98%，并相较原模型实现 2.01-2.47 倍端到端加速。
papers.tldr_zh: LoopZip 是一种无需训练的视觉 token 压缩方法，通过循环前视觉聚合、跨调用注意力平均选择和权重共享值校正，在循环 VLM 上以 50% 剪枝保留 97.16% 性能并显著降低显存与加速推理。

papers.title: Learning to Reason with Predictive Gains for Generative Recommendation
papers.abstract_en: Reasoning-enhanced generative recommendation (GR) has attracted increasing attention for leveraging the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) to improve next-item prediction. However, existing methods primarily optimize reasoning through Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with rule-based rewards determined by final recommendation performance, which faces two key limitations: (i) unmeasured predictive contributions within reasoning, where the predictive contributions of individual reasoning steps are not directly reflected in optimization signals, and (ii) weakly discriminative learning signals within groups, where different reasoning trajectories within the group often receive indistinguishable rewards, limiting effective policy optimization. In this paper, we propose GainReason, a simple yet effective training framework that optimizes reasoning through Predictive Gain (PG). Specifically, PG measures changes in target Semantic ID (SID) log-likelihood induced by individual reasoning sentences, providing contribution-aware and discriminative rewards. We further theoretically establish the alignment between expected PG and the recommendation ranking objective. Building on this signal, we develop PG-based Reasoning Optimization (PGRO) to optimize reasoning generation with sentence-level rewards, supported by a custom causal attention mechanism for efficient PG computation. Additionally, an auxiliary PG-based Reasoning Utilization (PGRU) task adaptively strengthens reasoning-conditioned prediction to complement PGRO. Extensive experiments on three public benchmarks demonstrate that GainReason consistently outperforms competitive baselines and achieves substantial performance gains from reasoning.
papers.abstract_zh: 推理增强的生成式推荐（GR）因利用大语言模型（LLM）的推理能力改进下一项预测而日益受到关注。然而，现有方法主要通过基于最终推荐性能的规则奖励进行组相对策略优化（GRPO）来优化推理，面临两个关键局限：（i）推理内部预测贡献未被度量，即单个推理步骤的预测贡献未直接反映在优化信号中；（ii）组内学习信号判别性弱，即组内不同推理轨迹往往获得难以区分的奖励，限制了有效的策略优化。本文提出GainReason，一个简单而有效的训练框架，通过预测增益（PG）优化推理。具体而言，PG度量单个推理句子引起的目标语义ID（SID）对数似然变化，提供贡献感知且具判别性的奖励。我们进一步从理论上建立了期望PG与推荐排序目标之间的对齐。基于该信号，我们开发了基于PG的推理优化（PGRO），以句子级奖励优化推理生成，并辅以自定义因果注意力机制以高效计算PG。此外，一个辅助的基于PG的推理利用（PGRU）任务自适应地增强以推理为条件的预测，以补充PGRO。在三个公开基准上的大量实验表明，GainReason持续优于竞争基线，并从推理中获得显著性能提升。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出GainReason，以单个推理句子引起的目标语义ID对数似然变化作为预测增益奖励，结合PGRO与PGRU优化推理生成，在三个公开基准上持续优于竞争基线。

papers.title: SpatialMind: Adaptive Multi-Level Geometric Fusion for Spatial Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) demonstrate promising capabilities in 2D visual understanding, yet remain limited in 3D spatial reasoning. Recent studies explore integrating 3D reconstruction models into MLLMs. However, these approaches either use a single geometric granularity across all tasks or adopt a fixed multi-level fusion scheme, regardless of task-specific reasoning requirements. Through systematic experiments on multi-level geometric fusion, we find that spatial tasks at different cognitive levels (e.g., distance estimation vs. route planning) require geometric representations of different granularities, revealing that fixed fusion cannot accommodate diverse spatial reasoning requirements. To bridge this gap, we propose SpatialMind, a task-adaptive framework for dynamically integrating multi-level geometric representations. SpatialMind employs GeoFus, a multi-layer geometric fusion module built around a gating network jointly conditioned on textual instructions, visual semantics, and geometric representations. This network adaptively modulates the contributions of shallow, intermediate, and deep geometric features across the layers of the LLM decoder. Furthermore, we introduce a negative-entropy regularization loss to mitigate gate collapse. Gate visualizations indicate that GeoFus adapts geometric granularity to task requirements. Experiments demonstrate that SpatialMind achieves competitive performance across spatial benchmarks, attaining a state-of-the-art score of 72.3 on VSI-Bench. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/zhaosb-star/SpatialMind.

papers.title: ReAccess: Look Once, Stay Focused with Efficient Test Time Memory
papers.abstract_en: Despite recent advances, vision-language models (VLMs) still struggle with fine-grained visual understanding, often failing to effectively utilize critical evidence already encoded in their visual representations. Existing approaches address this limitation through repeated visual processing or explicit reasoning, introducing substantial computational overhead. In this paper, we propose ReAccess, a lightweight framework that preserves and reuses question-relevant visual evidence through compact associative memory. Constructed during a single visual prefill, the memory supports progressive evidence retrieval that steers both attention queries and hidden representations, enabling effective visual grounding without repeated image encoding or explicit reasoning traces. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent improvements in both general visual understanding and fine-grained perception, while achieving substantially faster inference than existing reasoning-intensive approaches, demonstrating a promising path to efficient multimodal reasoning.
papers.abstract_zh: 尽管近期取得进展，视觉语言模型（VLM）在细粒度视觉理解上仍存在困难，往往未能有效利用其视觉表示中已编码的关键证据。现有方法通过重复视觉处理或显式推理来解决这一局限，带来大量计算开销。本文提出ReAccess，一个轻量级框架，通过紧凑的关联记忆保存并重用与问题相关的视觉证据。该记忆在单次视觉预填充期间构建，支持渐进式证据检索，引导注意力查询和隐藏表示，从而在无需重复图像编码或显式推理轨迹的情况下实现有效的视觉定位。大量实验表明，在通用视觉理解和细粒度感知上均取得一致改进，同时推理速度显著快于现有推理密集型方法，展示了高效多模态推理的有前景路径。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出ReAccess，在单次视觉预填充中构建紧凑关联记忆以保存并渐进检索问题相关视觉证据，引导注意力与隐藏表示，在通用和细粒度视觉理解上取得一致改进且推理显著快于推理密集型方法。

papers.title: Regularized Score Centering
papers.abstract_en: Asynchronous reinforcement learning increases training throughput, but data from stale policies and numerical mismatch between training and inference can destabilize learning. To stabilize off-policy learning, score centering (SC) removes the effect of reward baselines on the expected update. Our gradient diagnostics show less extreme gradients with SC than with importance sampling (IS), but SC can still fail when the learner moves far from the behavior policy that generated the data. To limit this policy mismatch, we introduce Regularized Score Centering (RSC), which adds a reverse Kullback-Leibler (KL) penalty to encourage the learner's next-token distribution to stay close to the behavior policy's next-token distribution. RSC works with or without truncated importance sampling (TIS), which caps token importance weights. Our theoretical analysis supports this approach, showing that KL regularization improves convergence guarantees. We evaluate dense and mixture-of-experts models on mathematical reasoning and agentic tasks, including online shopping, tool use, games, and fully asynchronous software engineering. RSC with TIS substantially improves sample efficiency across all agentic benchmarks, attaining higher training rewards with the same number of sampled responses. In final evaluations, it achieves top performance across all six agentic tasks, improving by 14.3% on AppWorld and reaching 9.9 times the strongest baseline's score on BabyAI.
papers.abstract_zh: 异步强化学习提高了训练吞吐量，但来自陈旧策略的数据以及训练与推理之间的数值不匹配可能使学习不稳定。为稳定离策略学习，分数中心化（score centering, SC）消除了奖励基线对期望更新的影响。我们的梯度诊断显示，SC 相比重要性采样（IS）产生的梯度更不极端，但当学习器远离生成数据的行為策略时，SC 仍可能失败。为限制这种策略不匹配，我们引入正则化分数中心化（Regularized Score Centering, RSC），它加入反向 Kullback-Leibler（KL）惩罚，促使学习器的下一词元分布接近行为策略的下一词元分布。RSC 可与截断重要性采样（TIS，限制词元重要性权重）配合使用，也可单独使用。我们的理论分析支持该方法，表明 KL 正则化改善了收敛保证。我们在数学推理和智能体任务（包括在线购物、工具使用、游戏和完全异步软件工程）上评估了稠密模型和专家混合模型。RSC 配合 TIS 在所有智能体基准上显著提升了样本效率，在相同采样回答数量下获得更高的训练奖励。在最终评估中，它在全部六个智能体任务上取得最佳性能，在 AppWorld 上提升 14.3%，在 BabyAI 上达到最强基线得分的 9.9 倍。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出正则化分数中心化RSC，在分数中心化基础上加入反向KL惩罚以限制与行为策略的偏差，理论分析表明其改善收敛保证，配合截断重要性采样在六个智能体任务上取得最佳性能，AppWorld提升14.3%。

papers.title: SpatialCast: Reading the 3D World via Cast Shadows
papers.abstract_en: As multimodal large language models (MLLMs) advance toward understanding and interacting with the physical world, spatial reasoning becomes essential for understanding scene structure and anticipating the effects of physical changes. Existing spatial benchmarks have made substantial progress in evaluating spatial relations, memory, and viewpoint reasoning, but less systematically assess how models connect physical scene conditions with visual observations. We introduce SpatialCast, a benchmark that uses cast shadows to evaluate this ability. Cast shadows provide observable evidence of a 3D scene. Their image appearance depends on object geometry and pose, illumination, and viewpoint. We examine this relationship through three complementary tasks that assess scene-projection consistency, predict intervention-induced changes, and infer the physical changes behind visual transitions. The benchmark contains 21,000 synthetic questions with separate scene and geometry test partitions, complemented by 200 SpatialCast-Real questions from 20 photographed scenes. Evaluations show that closed-source MLLMs outperform general-purpose open-weight MLLMs and MLLMs designed for spatial reasoning, which remain near chance on the synthetic benchmark, while even strong closed-source models struggle with shadow-length and light-height judgments. We also use SpatialCast training data for GRPO post-training, improving open-weight MLLM performance on the benchmark. Further evaluations show improvements on several external spatial benchmarks, suggesting transfer of the learned capabilities. These experiments support SpatialCast as a controlled resource for diagnosing spatial reasoning capabilities and studying their learning and generalization.

papers.title: BaseRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of a Base Vision-Language Model via Training-Free Harness Internalization
papers.abstract_en: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) is moving from the harness of prompts and tools around a base model toward the model itself. However, existing RSI still faces key challenges, including harness-bound gains that stay outside the base model, black-box supervision that reads only the model's outputs, and imprecise edits whose site and strength are fixed in advance. To address these challenges, we propose BaseRSI, a new paradigm of Recursive Harness Internalization: the base model improves its harness, then writes what the harness adds into its own weights through training-free edits, round after round on its own responses. To support this paradigm, we introduce ReGap, a mechanism that supervises every transformer block with the high-dimensional activation difference that the harness makes at that block alone, and updates the block's weights along this signal in a low-dimensional subspace. Building on this mechanism, we further propose ReKey, an algorithm that writes this signal by regression into a few key-value neurons of every block, and measures the site and strength of each edit on the model's own responses. Moreover, the base model fills every role of this recursion with forward passes alone, and its edits, written at different sites, compose in one checkpoint without refitting. Experimental results on ten visual reasoning benchmarks show that BaseRSI consistently improves a base vision-language model both in distribution and on held-out benchmarks. Our code is available at https://github.com/beita6969/BaseRSI.

papers.title: OAK-Mind: Zero-Training Mental Health Change Inference from Passive Sensing via Knowledge-Grounded Multi-Agent LLMs
papers.abstract_en: Wearable and smartphone sensors capture behavioral signals associated with mental health, yet inferring mental health outcomes from these signals has traditionally relied on supervised models requiring labeled data and offering limited insight into their predictions. Large language models (LLMs) offer new opportunities to reason over behavioral evidence, but existing LLM-based approaches to passive sensing have largely continued to rely on task-specific fine-tuning or sensor-specific pretraining. In this paper, we introduce OAK-Mind, a zerO-training, multi-Agent, Knowledge-grounded LLM pipeline for inferring mental health changes from passive sensing data. The pipeline organizes sensing data into behavioral dimensions including sleep, physical activity, location mobility, and smartphone use, and orchestrates specialized agents grounded in mental health literature to interpret longitudinal behavioral changes. It synthesizes their assessments and applies questionnaire-based symptom rating to infer changes relative to an individual's baseline assessment with human-readable rationale grounded in observed behavioral patterns and domain knowledge. Across datasets and prediction tasks, while without task-specific training, OAK-Mind achieves comparable or better performance than the most predictive supervised baselines trained on additional labeled samples. It also demonstrate consistent improvement upon direct prompting across four tested LLM backbones. Ablation analyses support the benefits of combining behavioral interpretation with symptom rating, distributing analysis across domain-specific agents, and incorporating domain knowledge. Our findings highlight the potential of knowledge-grounded, multi-agent LLMs for training-free inference of mental health changes from passive sensing data.

papers.title: DailyBrick: Language-Guided Synthesis of Brick Assembly Instructions
papers.abstract_en: Generating a LEGO model from a user request is more than a plausible 3D shape generation. LEGO models require physical support per brick, and each brick should be placed unblocked. Current methods address this issue by training an expert large language model. We reduce the problem of generating extremely long context on all brick connections to that of writing a program that builds LEGO models like a human, considering each intermediate step could be executed. We introduce DailyBrick , a multi-stage agentic system that produces a LEGO model together with a brick-by-brick assembly instruction for human building and robot assembly. We design a multi-stage harness with roles to help LLMs generate more effectively. A versioned construction SDK compiles multi-level decisions, from semantic subparts to individual bricks, into canonical operations. An external Meta-Reviewer agent replays and inspects the generated package, verifies the model and its construction process, identifies failures, traces them to the responsible stage, and routes them to bounded repairs or to editable candidates for later skill or tool updates. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DailyBrick generates LEGO models based on simple user requests better than recent agentic systems, and show its utility in downstream applications such as robot manipulations on model assembly from instructions and brick sets (https://SpatialAgent.github.io/DailyBrick/).
papers.abstract_zh: 根据用户请求生成 LEGO 模型，不只是生成一个看似合理的 3D 形状。LEGO 模型要求每块积木都有物理支撑，且每块积木的放置不应被阻挡。当前方法通过训练专家大语言模型来解决该问题。我们将生成所有积木连接这一超长上下文的问题，简化为编写一个像人类一样搭建 LEGO 模型的程序，并考虑每个中间步骤都可执行。我们提出 DailyBrick，一个多阶段智能体系统，可生成 LEGO 模型以及逐块搭建说明，供人类搭建和机器人装配使用。我们设计了一个带角色的多阶段执行框架，帮助 LLM 更有效地生成。一个版本化构建 SDK 将多层级决策（从语义子部件到单块积木）编译为规范操作。外部 Meta-Reviewer 智能体回放并检查生成的包，验证模型及其构建过程，识别失败，追溯至负责阶段，并将其路由到有界修复或可编辑候选，以供后续技能或工具更新。大量实验表明，DailyBrick 能基于简单用户请求生成优于近期智能体系统的 LEGO 模型，并展示了其在机器人按说明和积木套装进行模型装配等下游应用中的效用（https://SpatialAgent.github.io/DailyBrick/）。

papers.title: SARVIA: Fast-Adapting the Strong SAR Foundation Models That Are Already in Your MLLMs
papers.abstract_en: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) foundation models provide transferable representations for diverse perception tasks in all-weather Earth observation. However, their development often relies on costly large-scale SAR pretraining, raising the question of whether such extensive domain-specific pretraining is necessary. We find that modern multimodal large language models (MLLMs) already provide visual encoders that can outperform dedicated SAR foundation models as downstream initializations. This motivates a new paradigm: reuse general visual capabilities and devote domain training to brief specialization. We therefore introduce SARVIA, an adaptive post-pretraining method that specializes modern MLLMs using self-supervised visual questions with computable answers. These questions are constructed from unlabeled observations through general image tasks that capture spatial relations and SAR-specific tasks that exploit native measurements and SAR--optical correspondence. A shared answer-prediction objective jointly trains low-rank adapters across visual and language components, with loss-driven task sampling. We then export the adapted visual encoder as a standalone backbone. With 600 adaptation steps and 2 GPU-hours, SARVIA outperforms the compared foundation models on all six SAR detection and segmentation benchmarks. Compared with dedicated SAR pretraining, SARVIA reduces domain-training costs by orders of magnitude while improving visual transfer across architectures and scales. This new paradigm shifts the emphasis from repeated, costly pretraining to a reusable specialization process that can benefit from advances in open MLLMs. Dataset and code: https://github.com/zcablii/SARVIA.

papers.title: Keep the Reasoning, Read the Image: On-Demand Visual KV for Multi-Turn Reasoning VLMs
papers.abstract_en: Reasoning vision-language models (VLMs) think for thousands of tokens before they answer, and retention policies keep the KV cache affordable by pruning it as the reasoning grows. We find that this pruning sacrifices the image in multi-turn conversations: the image and the reasoning share one budget, so the growing reasoning crowds the visual entries out. A chart question that loses 8 points to the full cache when asked first loses 24 points when asked after a round of reasoning. Protecting a small visual reserve from eviction recovers most of this loss, while adding the same slots to the shared budget recovers considerably less. The image therefore lacks protection, not capacity. Based on this finding, we propose ShelfKV, a training-free method that works on top of existing retention policies. It keeps every visual entry in CPU memory and, at each decoding step, swaps the visual entries that the current query scores highest into the attention slots of the text entries it scores lowest. The image is never evicted, yet it occupies attention slots only while it is read. We evaluate ShelfKV on four benchmarks, three of them conversational, with two retention policies and two reasoning VLMs. In conversations, it improves the strongest existing policy, DBTrimKV, by up to 20.3 points at matched GPU memory, and still leads by 8.7 points when DBTrimKV uses twice the memory. It also consistently outperforms a fixed visual reserve of matched GPU memory in these settings, without hurting accuracy on standalone questions. These results show that the image should be protected from the reasoning but read only on demand.

papers.title: M3OPD-Reasoner: An Open Recipe for Post-Training Multimodal Reasoning with Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract_en: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD) enables a single student to absorb the skills of several domain teachers by learning from its own generated responses. We present Multimodal Model Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation Reasoner (M3OPD-Reasoner), a fully open recipe for post-training vision-language models (VLMs) over three reasoning domains: image STEM, image perception, and video. We curate two datasets, M3OPD-SFT-1.35M for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and M3OPD-RL-193K for reinforcement learning (RL) with verifiable rewards. On these data, we compare post-training recipes that start from Qwen3.5-9B: training one model on the mixed data of all domains (MixSFT and MixRL), and training one teacher per domain with Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO), directly or after an SFT warm-up, and distilling the teachers into one student with MOPD. We evaluate on 21 image STEM, image perception, and video reasoning benchmarks after we decontaminate the training data against them. The comparison establishes MOPD of teachers trained with GSPO directly from Qwen3.5-9B as the best recipe: the student closely matches each teacher on its own domain and is on average above the mixed-training baselines on the same prompts. Since MOPD already merges the domain capabilities that MixRL would otherwise have to learn, its student is a stronger starting point for RL, and we ask whether the same data can carry the model further from there: we add MixRL on top of the MOPD student, on the same prompts and with the same settings, which, to our knowledge, no prior VLM recipe has studied. The same prompts still improve the MOPD student, with no collapse, and give our main model, M3OPD-Reasoner-9B. MOPD and MixRL can therefore work as consecutive stages that get more out of the same data. We release all data, the training code, and the checkpoints of every stage.

papers.title: Sample-efficient Personalization of Large Language Model Alignment with Multidimensional User Preference Data
papers.abstract_en: Preference alignment has become a central tool to align large language models (LLMs) with human values and desired behavior, and its online variant can further advance their capabilities beyond what static data alone offer by repeatedly generating and labeling new responses with human feedback. But costly, time-consuming annotations limit its scalability, making sample efficiency essential, and existing methods typically seek to improve it by expanding coverage of the response space or selecting pairs with the highest uncertainty for comparison. Although they are effective, these methods quantify uncertainty from the perspective of the LLM, which may differ from the uncertainty perceived by the user: a pair can appear highly uncertain to the LLM even when past comparisons from the user already imply a clear ordering. In this paper, we propose multidimensional preference-guided online direct preference optimization (MPG-DPO), which leverages low-cost multidimensional evaluations from automated verifiers on the user historical comparisons to construct a personalized preference cone guiding response selection for online preference alignment. Specifically, it first discards responses that are confidently dominated under the estimated user preference, then selects two responses that are competitive under the retained preference cone yet exhibit the strongest unresolved disagreement. Theoretical analysis shows that, with high probability, the fraction of queries spent on cone-dominated responses vanishes as learning progresses. Experiments across multiple LLM families show that MPG-DPO outperforms strong contenders under matched query budgets.

papers.title: When AUC Meets Generative Reconstruction: A Unified Principle for Balanced Visual Representation Learning
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) require visual encoders that extract fine-grained visual features while constructing semantically disentangled and discriminative representations. Conventional methodologies encounter a fundamental trade-off: contrastive learning enhances inter-class discrimination by suppressing intra-class variability, whereas generative reconstruction emphasizes perceptual fidelity but lacks explicit comparative supervision. The naive aggregation of these objectives via composite loss functions often induces optimization conflicts and instability due to gradient interference within the shared latent space. To resolve this, we introduce a unified representation-learning paradigm that reformulates generative reconstruction as a discriminative ranking problem within the generative output manifold. Our approach maintains perceptual reconstruction as a supervisory signal and integrates a ranking-based discriminative constraint by systematically ordering matched and mismatched reconstruction outputs. This formulation embeds discriminative information seamlessly into the generative process, alleviating the risk of loss competition. Specifically, we propose AUC Generative Reconstruction (AUCGR), which optimizes the area under the ROC curve (AUC) by ensuring higher scores for matched pairs than for mismatched pairs, and Partial AUC Generative Reconstruction (pAUCGR), which addresses supervision bias by focusing on mismatched comparisons within reliable feature subspaces. The proposed objectives are designed to be plug-and-play, requiring no architectural modifications to existing generative reconstruction frameworks. Theoretical analysis establishes rigorous connections to AUC/pAUC optimization and provides generalization guarantees. Extensive experiments validate that our method advances both discriminative accuracy and fine-grained perceptual representation.

papers.title: MemDoctor: Stage-wise Error Attribution and Repair for MLLM Agent Memory
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) now assist users across sessions of images and text, carried by an external memory of what was said and shown. When such an assistant answers wrongly, the failure usually began earlier, in how a record was written, updated or retrieved, and the answer alone does not say where. We formalize multimodal memory as four stages, Write, Update, Retrieve and Answer, and define nine error types across them. A stage-resolved analysis on Mem-Gallery traces most failures to a source stage, and most of those lie before the answer. Injecting known errors against fact-preserving control edits, we then follow each tainted record downstream. Early errors survive to the answer as apparent evidence, and hurt most when no other record holds the fact. A diagnosis that trusts the quoted evidence therefore blames the stage where the error surfaces, not the one where it began. We propose MemDoctor, in which the MLLM that built the memory diagnoses its own failures. It traces each needed fact backward through the four stages, accepts a diagnosis only when the cited evidence is found in memory, and repairs that stage before answering again. On a 4B backbone, MemDoctor improves accuracy on both Mem-Gallery and MemLens, outperforming all evaluated 8B baselines, and the same loop also improves MuRAG and A-Mem.

papers.title: AggCLIP: Aggregating CLIP for Zero-Shot Multimodal Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract_en: Zero-Shot Multimodal Anomaly Detection (ZSMAD) aims to identify both appearance and geometric defects in novel categories without relying on target-specific training data, making it especially valuable in real-world scenarios constrained by data scarcity, privacy concerns, or high annotation costs. While recent approaches successfully adapt vision-language models like CLIP to achieve this open-vocabulary generalization, they still face significant challenges: (i) severe geometric information loss during 3D-to-2D point cloud rendering; (ii) spatially noisy 2D feature maps produced by raw CLIP patch embeddings, compounded by shallow late-stage modality fusion; and (iii) severe cross-modal semantic misalignment due to decoupled processing streams. To address these limitations, we propose AggCLIP, a novel framework that adapts frozen CLIP representations for ZSMAD by explicitly incorporating local geometric structure and visual spatial context. Specifically, to accurately localize fine-grained defects, we design a Geometry-Aware Spatial Aggregation (GSA) module that refines back-projected 3D point features via density-adaptive neighborhood weighting, alongside a Context-Aware Spatial Aggregation (CSA) module that smooths multi-scale 2D patch embeddings using a lightweight trainable adapter. Furthermore, to prevent semantic drift between modalities, we introduce a Dual-Stream Prompt Contrastive (DSPC) loss, which aligns the abstract concepts of normality and abnormality across the point cloud and RGB streams. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed AggCLIP framework achieves state-of-the-art performance on the MVTec 3D-AD and Eyecandies benchmarks under both one-vs-rest and cross-dataset zero-shot settings, notably surpassing the strongest competitive methods by up to 2.9% in pixel-level AUPRO.

papers.title: CROMPT: Adapting CLIP via Cross-Modal Prompting for Robust Zero-Shot Generalization under Adverse Weather
papers.abstract_en: Domain adaptation for semantic segmentation is challenging when target-domain images are unavailable during training. Zero-shot domain adaptation addresses this by adapting models using only textual descriptions of the target domain. However, existing prompt-learning methods are not well suited for ResNet-based CLIP vision backbones or pixel-level cross-modal feature alignment. We propose CROMPT, a prompt-learning framework for zero-shot domain adaptation in semantic segmentation. CROMPT introduces Cross-Modal Feature Augmentation (CROMA), combining Random Visual Prompting with Hybrid Textual Prompting (HTP) to jointly adapt visual and textual representations. We further propose CROMA-VL, which leverages vision-language models to generate domain-conditioned prompts, and a progressive easy-to-hard adaptation strategy for improved domain invariance. Experiments on two benchmark datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over strong baselines and state-of-the-art methods, achieving 1.63-2.63% mIoU gains while maintaining inference-time complexity. These results establish CROMPT as an effective and efficient framework for zero-shot multi-domain semantic segmentation. OpenReview: https://openreview.net/forum?id=FxqFsIL685

papers.title: [CLS] and [EOS] Tokens are not Enough for CLIP-based Class-Incremental Learning
papers.abstract_en: Class-Incremental Learning (CIL) aims to empower models to continuously acquire new knowledge while mitigating catastrophic forgetting. With the advent of vision-language models like CLIP, leveraging their cross-modal alignment capabilities to address CIL challenges has emerged as a dominant paradigm. Existing methods leverage CLIP's global representations (i.e., the visual [CLS] token and the textual [EOS] token) for cross-modal alignment. While achieving effective classification, they overlook the rich patch-level visual features and token-level textual semantics inherent in CLIP. For example, the [CLS] token aggregates local information to capture the general concept of "cat", while the patch-level details retain specific localized features essential for recognition, such as the tail, fur, and face. We propose PACE (PAtch-token Cross-modal Enhancement) to uncover the long-neglected local representations within CLIP. First, based on the global representations like [CLS] token and [EOS] token, we identify the top-k most crucial visual patches and textual tokens. Subsequently, to better utilize the extracted key local features, we design a cross-modal fusion module. This module leverages local textual semantics to refine visual representations, while augmenting textual semantics with local visual features. As the fusion module is shared across all tasks, directly fine-tuning it on new tasks would interfere with the knowledge learned from previous tasks, leading to catastrophic forgetting. To alleviate this, we employ a projection-based update strategy to effectively preserve the critical parameter space of previous tasks during the adaptation to new tasks. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PACE significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods across multiple CIL benchmarks.

papers.title: Towards Reliable Scaling Laws for Tabular Foundation Models
papers.abstract_en: Scaling laws are widely used to predict foundation model performance and guide compute allocation. However, tabular foundation models (TFMs) differ from conventional foundation models in that they are pretrained on virtually unlimited synthetic data from configurable distributions, while ultimately being evaluated on real-world datasets. We investigate whether scaling laws for TabPFNv2-style models reliably extrapolate to larger compute budgets and generalize across evaluation settings. Our analysis reveals differences between synthetic and real-world scaling behavior and shows that accurately fitting a scaling law does not necessarily yield reliable prescriptions on unseen datasets. In particular, selecting configurations using too few evaluation datasets leads to systematically over-optimistic performance estimates. We further demonstrate that compute-optimal scaling requires expanding the range of synthetic pretraining dataset sizes alongside model size and training compute. Increasing the maximum numbers of rows and features sampled during pretraining improves performance and produces more predictable scaling trends. These insights guide the training of more efficient TabPFNv2-like models, using the open-source training pipeline of nanoTabPFN.

papers.title: Let a Small Model Read First: Faster Prefill for Long Interleaved Image-Text Inputs
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language models (VLMs) can answer questions about long interleaved inputs, such as documents of many pages and collections of hundreds of images, but they are slow to start: on inputs of about 100K tokens, the prefill takes most of the wait for the first output token. A common approach prunes the input by scoring its tokens with the target model itself or with a small model of the same family that first writes an answer. However, this scoring takes much of the time that pruning saves. We find that the evidence for a question lies in a few whole units (images or paragraphs), and that a small hybrid model finds them with one attention head of an early layer, even at half image resolution. Based on these findings, we propose SkimPrefill, which lets the small hybrid model read the whole input first, up to that early layer, with images at half resolution. Most layers of the small hybrid model (Qwen3.5-0.8B) run in linear time, so this pass is short. SkimPrefill then ranks every unit with that head and gives the target the top units as an ordinary shorter prompt. One untrained selector serves targets of different model families. Extensive experiments on MMLongBench at 128K tokens, with 19 datasets of five task types, show the effectiveness of SkimPrefill. With 10% of the input tokens kept, SkimPrefill speeds up the prefill of Qwen3.5-9B, Gemma-4-12B and Qwen3-VL-32B by 3.7 times, 11.6 time and 8.2 times while maintaining their average accuracy.

papers.title: APS: Adaptive Partitioning-Based Frame Selection for Long Video Understanding
papers.abstract_en: Recent advances in large vision-language models (LVLMs) have significantly improved video understanding capabilities, yet processing long videos remains challenging due to the substantial computational cost of extensive visual inputs. Frame selection offers an efficient alternative, but many existing region-based methods rely on fixed or predefined temporal partitions, which may result in suboptimal temporal regions, compromising subsequent budget allocation and frame selection. In this work, we propose Adaptive Partitioning-Based Frame Selection (APS), a training-free framework that adapts temporal partitions to local variations in query-frame relevance. Specifically, APS formulates temporal partitioning as a complexity-regularized fitting problem, jointly optimizing partition boundaries and local models through dynamic programming. The resulting adaptive temporal partitions guide frame budget allocation based on query relevance and temporal extent, enabling informative frame selection under limited visual budgets. Extensive experiments on Video-MME, MLVU, and LongVideoBench demonstrate that APS consistently improves performance across diverse LVLM backbones, achieving the highest average gains over uniform sampling among competing methods. Further analyses validate the effectiveness of adaptive partitioning and demonstrate its generalizability across model scales, similarity encoders, and advanced LVLMs.

papers.title: Tracking Representations in LLM Reasoning Traces for Iterated Games
papers.abstract_en: Large language model (LLM) agents achieve state-of-the-art performance across domains through chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning. Despite their ubiquitous use, little is understood about the relationship between the externalized trace and the model's actual computation. We address this by investigating how LLM agents make decisions in iterative games with incomplete information. Using a series of mechanistic interpretability techniques, we find that the model forms and iteratively revises an internal representation of the game throughout the CoT. Once the model prematurely commits to an incorrect belief, it rarely recovers. This failure is manifested in both the literal trace and the layer activations. Ultimately, as multi-agent systems are more prevalent, our work opens the door to a more focused diagnosis of their strategic reasoning errors. For illustrative purposes, we offer an interactive visualizer of our methodology on selected sample traces at https://interp-self.github.io/gametrace/

papers.title: Teaching What to Look For: Privileged Perception Questions for Agentic On-Policy Distillation in Video Captioning
papers.abstract_en: Detailed video captioning requires comprehensive and faithful descriptions of objects, actions, and temporal events. Fixed-frame sampling, however, can miss brief motions, small objects, and other fine-grained evidence, motivating captioning agents that actively seek relevant moments and inspect local regions. Training such behavior is challenging because, unlike video question answering, generic captioning instructions do not specify what visual evidence should be acquired. We propose Perception-Question On-Policy Distillation (PQ-OPD), which uses training-only Perception Questions (PQs) to guide active video perception. PQs specify what should be inspected without revealing the corresponding answers, encouraging the teacher to explore the video more comprehensively and focus on relevant visual evidence. Along trajectories generated by the student, on-policy distillation transfers this guidance to the student's reasoning, tool calls, and captions; no PQs are required at inference. Across three detailed-captioning and two caption-to-QA benchmarks, PQ-OPD consistently improves the corresponding untrained agents across teacher-student scales and input-frame budgets. Under our evaluation protocol, PQ-OPD achieves the strongest primary-metric results among the compared open-source models on DREAM-1K, CaReBench, ShortVidBench, MotionBench, and VidCapBench-AE. Our ablations, together with analysis of temporal coverage and answer leakage, further indicates that the student internalizes the training-time guidance as a more effective video exploration policy.

papers.title: Beyond Token Stacking: Multi-scale Visual Modulation and Adaptive Fused-feature Calibration for MLLMs
papers.abstract_en: Current Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have advanced rapidly and follow two main paradigms: one involves concatenating visual and textual tokens for input into Large Language Model (LLM), while the other injects visual knowledge into Feed-Forward Networks (FFNs) of the LLM. However, the former introduces a large number of redundant visual tokens, substantially increasing computational overhead. The latter reduces sequence length but removes images from the input stage entirely, which may hinder the activation of image-related knowledge. Moreover, naively injecting visual knowledge into the FFNs could induce activation distribution shifts due to cross-modal semantic discrepancies. To address these challenges, we develop Beyond Token Stacking (BTS), a novel visual enhancement framework for MLLMs. Specifically, we propose a Multi-scale Visual Modulation (MVM) mechanism that injects multi-scale visual information at the input stage via modulation without increasing the token sequence length. Furthermore, we develop an Adaptive Fused-feature Calibration (AFC) module that performs per-channel affine calibration to decouple visual injection from distribution alignment in the FFN layers, improving multimodal fusion stability while preserving language priors. Experiments show that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance.
